Around the schemas Open mHealth ships a stack of Apache-2.0 reference implementations: Shimmer (a Java/Spring server that pulls health data from Fitbit, Google Fit, iHealth, Misfit, RunKeeper, and Withings APIs and normalizes it into Open mHealth or IEEE 1752.1 data points), omh-dsu-ri (a Data Storage Unit reference implementation exposing an OAuth 2.0-secured Data Point REST API on top of MongoDB and PostgreSQL), Granola (an Objective-C library that serializes Apple HealthKit samples into Open mHealth JSON), a web visualizations library built on D3 and Plottable.js, the OMH-on-FHIR mapping that aligns Open mHealth data points to HL7 FHIR resources, and a sample-data-generator. Open mHealth operates as the steward of the standard, the schema and unit registry at registry.openmhealth.org, and a developer community of thousands of developers and health organizations including Cornell Tech, Kaiser Permanente, Stanford School of Medicine, UC Davis, and UCSF. The project has no commercial API, no paid tier, and no hosted SaaS — all artifacts are open source under Apache 2.0 and the standard itself is openly published.

providers.name: Forward Platform
providers.description: FORWARD Platform is a govtech SaaS company (a Techstars portfolio company) offering one secure platform for administering public-benefit programs. It serves governments, nonprofits, and foundations with tooling for program management, online form building, eligibility determination, case management, client communication, referrals, payment disbursement, reporting and analytics, and fraud prevention. FORWARD supports service-delivery programs such as guaranteed basic income, housing assistance, and emergency management, and is packaged in Direct, Pro, Enterprise, and Ally tiers. Enrichment found no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, MCP server, or developer portal — this is a product/marketing web presence only.

providers.name: Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts (PAFA)
providers.description: The Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts (PAFA) is the United States' first museum and school of fine arts, founded in 1805 in Philadelphia by painter and scientist Charles Willson Peale, sculptor William Rush, and other artists and business leaders. PAFA operates as a 501(c)(3) cultural nonprofit at 118-128 North Broad Street, Philadelphia, PA 19102 and occupies two connected historic buildings — the Frank Furness and George Hewitt-designed Furness-Hewitt Building (1876, designated a National Historic Landmark in 1975) and the Samuel M. V. Hamilton Building — joined by Lenfest Plaza. PAFA's permanent collection focuses on 19th- and 20th-century American art and includes works tied to alumni and faculty such as Mary Cassatt, Thomas Eakins, Henry Ossawa Tanner, William Glackens, Barkley L. Hendricks, Violet Oakley, Cecilia Beaux, Louis Kahn, David Lynch, and Njideka Akunyili Crosby, alongside the Linda Lee Alter Collection of Art by Women. Following a March 2025 announcement of a financial crisis driven by a reported roughly $3 million annual deficit and a sharp decline in enrollment, PAFA stopped granting its own BFA and MFA degrees beginning with the 2024-2025 academic year. As of 2026 the school's active educational pathways are the three-year Fine Arts Certificate Program ("designed to prepare students for entry-level professional roles within the visual arts and related creative industries"), Continuing Education classes ("an inclusive studio arts offering for artists of all ages and skill levels, from beginners to advanced creatives") delivered in-person and online, Youth & Teen programs including Summer Art Camp and Summer Academy, and PAFA Shop Memberships providing self-guided access to professional-grade printmaking, papermaking, and sculpture studios. The museum continues to operate, with admission $25 adults / $23 seniors / $10 students / $5 youth / free for children 12 and under and members, and is presenting the once-in-a-generation exhibition "A Nation of Artists" (April 2026 - September 2027) in partnership with the Philadelphia Museum of Art and the Middleton Family Collection. PAFA is a cultural nonprofit, not a technology company. It publishes no developer portal, no OpenAPI specifications, no SDKs, no public REST or GraphQL APIs, no webhooks, no status page, and no engineering blog. There is no `github.com/pafa` institutional organization — the user account `github.com/pafa` is an unrelated personal account focused on ERP and WeChat tooling. The institution's only programmatic third-party surface is its participation in the Bloomberg Connects free digital museum guide app, which presents PAFA's collection and tours through Bloomberg Philanthropies' shared mobile platform. Donations are routed through the third-party platform community.pafa.org/give and ticketing through standard museum e-commerce.

providers.name: Democracy Earth
providers.description: Democracy Earth Foundation is a Y Combinator- and Fast Forward-backed 501(c)(3) nonprofit building free, open-source, blockchain-based software for incorruptible digital governance and voting. Its flagship Sovereign application is a liquid-democracy platform that lets communities vote directly on issues or delegate their voting power to trusted peers over a decentralized, censorship-resistant network. The Foundation also develops self-sovereign identity (a proof-of-humanity protocol), a universal basic income token, and a minimal quadratic-voting DAO, publishing all of its work as open-source repositories rather than as a commercial, hosted API. Democracy Earth is a protocol-first, decentralized project without a hosted REST API or developer program.

providers.name: Grassroots Unwired
providers.description: Grassroots Unwired is a mobile-first platform for face-to-face (F2F) outreach, advocacy, and fundraising, purpose-built for political campaigns, nonprofits, labor unions, and community organizations. Its offline-capable mobile apps let field teams run GPS-enabled door-to-door canvassing, capture in-person and peer-to-peer donations, send SMS and digital content from the field, and manage event check-in, registration, and merchandise operations for 4EventDay. The platform keeps collecting data, donations, and check-ins even when Wi-Fi and cell coverage are spotty, then syncs in real time with major CRM, donor, and payment systems (EveryAction, NGP VAN, Blackbaud Luminate, NeonCRM, Stripe, and others).

providers.name: The Human Utility
providers.description: The Human Utility (formerly the Detroit Water Project) is a Y Combinator-backed not-for-profit organization founded in 2014 by Tiffani Ashley Bell whose mission is to preserve human dignity by increasing water affordability for families across the United States. It matches families who are behind on their water bills with donors who want to help, paying utility companies directly on their behalf through crowdfunded donations, community-building, and policy action. Operating in Detroit, Baltimore, and dozens of other cities, it has helped thousands of households avoid water shutoffs. The Human Utility runs a public-facing web application for donors and recipients rather than a developer-facing API product; its source code lives in the humanutility GitHub organization. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched with identity and link details; no public API surface was found.

providers.name: Monell Chemical Senses Center
providers.description: The Monell Chemical Senses Center is "the world's only independent, non-profit scientific institute dedicated to interdisciplinary basic research on the senses of taste and smell." Founded in 1968 and headquartered in Philadelphia, Monell conducts chemosensory research organized around three strategic themes: Healthy Senses and Happy Lives, Senses for a Thriving Planet, and Nourishing Our Future. The center runs postdoctoral training, the Dr. Charis Eng Monell Science Apprenticeship Program, the Monell Science Entrepreneurship Program, an Academic Partnership Program, and the Monell Insiders corporate partnership program. Monell does not publish a public developer API surface; its "product" is knowledge disseminated through scholarly publications and conferences.

providers.name: Noora Health
providers.description: Noora Health is a healthcare nonprofit that turns the time patients and their families spend in hospitals into an opportunity to learn high-impact health skills. Working through public and private health systems across South Asia, its Care Companion Program trains family caregivers at the bedside so they can care for their loved ones after discharge, reducing preventable complications and readmissions. Founded in 2014 and a Y Combinator-backed organization, Noora Health operates in India, Bangladesh, Indonesia, and Nepal and has trained tens of millions of caregivers and patients. It is a mission-driven organization rather than an API provider, and no public developer portal, API, or SDK surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: ChurchTrac
providers.description: ChurchTrac is all-in-one church management software (ChMS) for small and large churches, covering people and member management, church directory, groups, attendance and check-in, event registration, worship planning and volunteer scheduling, online giving, and fund accounting/budgeting. ChurchTrac does NOT publish a public or partner developer API - there is no documented REST API, API keys, OAuth, or webhooks for building against ChurchTrac data. Its "integrations" are ChurchTrac consuming third-party services (Stripe for giving, SendGrid/Mailchimp for email, Twilio for texting, QuickBooks for accounting, Zoom); member-facing access is via the Church Connect app and embeddable online giving forms, not a programmable API surface. This entry is documented as an honest stub.

providers.name: Arc Institute
providers.description: Arc Institute is an independent nonprofit biomedical research organization headquartered in Palo Alto, California, co-founded in 2021 by Silvana Konermann (Executive Director), Patrick Hsu (Core Investigator), and Stripe co-founder Patrick Collison. With 300+ staff ("Arconauts") across 9 core laboratories and 5 technology centers, Arc develops AI foundation models for biology that span DNA, RNA, proteins, and single cells. Its flagship releases include Evo (Science, 2024) and Evo 2 (Nature, 2026) — DNA foundation models trained on trillions of nucleotides at single-nucleotide resolution with up to a 1-megabase context; STATE and Stack single-cell foundation models for cellular perturbation and in-context learning; the Arc Virtual Cell Atlas; the SRAgent LLM agents for bioinformatics; and the BINSEQ binary sequencing format. Models are released under Apache 2.0 on GitHub and Hugging Face, with hosted inference for Evo 2 available through NVIDIA BioNeMo and the NVIDIA build.nvidia.com API. Arc is funded by philanthropic donations from Patrick and John Collison, Vitalik Buterin, the Ron Conway family, Dustin Moskovitz, Daniel Gross, Elad Gil, and other technology benefactors; it does not sell APIs, SaaS, or models commercially.

providers.name: OpenCola
providers.description: OpenCola is a non-profit organization building free, open-source, local-first software as an alternative to corporate social media and cloud platforms. Its application keeps a user's data on their own device by default, offering personal search, offline content archives, multiple personas, trust-based connections via tokens, information-centric collaboration, and community moderation. The project is grounded in four principles: transparency, accountability, personal control, and security (cryptographic verification). It is a revival of the original OpenCola (1999), and the current release is a local desktop application rather than a hosted service. OpenCola publishes no public web API, developer portal, SDK, or OpenAPI at this time; this profile captures its identity and open-source posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Go Deed
providers.description: Go Deed (legally Deed Inc.) is a workplace-giving and corporate social responsibility platform founded in 2016 that helps enterprises engage employees around volunteering, charitable giving, donation matching, and everyday social-impact actions. With teams in New York, San Francisco, and Berlin, Deed served Fortune 500 and mid-market employers before being acquired into Bonterra, where it now ships as the "Deed" employee-engagement product. The joindeed.com domain 301-redirects to bonterratech.com/product/deed. Deed was surfaced as an Earlybird Venture Capital portfolio company (investment 2021) and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. Enrichment found no independent public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API specification for the standalone Go Deed / Deed brand.

providers.name: OpenToken
providers.description: OpenToken (OpenToken Inc.) was a San Francisco based cryptocurrency startup founded in 2017 that operated a token-fundraising and token-project aggregation platform, generating a secure, per-buyer funding address for each contributor so token projects could collect and distribute assets during their sales. The company was backed by Bain Capital Ventures, Pantera Capital, and Moonwhale Ventures. It is no longer active: the opentoken.com domain is parked (it refuses HTTPS connections and resolves to OnlyDomains parking nameservers), and no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable API specification, or first-party SDK could be located for the company. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Pantera Capital and remains a defunct-company record in the API Evangelist network; there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: WeDidIt
providers.description: WeDidIt was a Brooklyn, New York fundraising platform founded in 2012 by Su Sanni and Benjamin Lamson that gave small nonprofits online donation pages, crowdfunding, peer-to-peer, ticketing, and fiscal-sponsorship tools, plus a mobile app for in-person card donations. A 500 Global portfolio company and 43North winner, it was acquired by Allegiance Fundraising Group in June 2019 and its product folded into the Allegiance suite. No public developer API was ever documented, and the wedid.it domain has since lapsed to an unrelated site, so no API surface remains to profile.

providers.name: Win-Win
providers.description: Win-Win (trywinwin.com) is a charitable-fundraising platform that gamifies giving. Participants compete in tournaments hosted by celebrities and influencers, predicting head-to-head matchup outcomes and making tax-deductible donations to charitable causes while climbing leaderboards to win prizes and experiences. Win-Win also offers B2B tooling for nonprofits and corporations to launch their own gamified fundraising campaigns, alongside a consumer mobile app. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. No public API or developer surface is currently published.

providers.name: Mentor Spaces
providers.description: Mentor Spaces is a structured mentorship platform that helps nonprofits, universities, and companies launch, manage, and measure mentorship programs at scale. The software handles automated mentor-mentee matching, scheduling, communication, and real-time outcome tracking so organizations can secure and renew grant funding with funder-ready impact reports, improve student persistence and career outcomes, engage alumni in time-bound structured mentorship, and run skills-based volunteering and corporate CSR/ESG programs. A public developer API and custom integrations are offered only on the enterprise Thrive tier (with SSO); no public API documentation is published. Founded by Chris Motley and backed by Techstars.

providers.name: Givecampus
providers.description: GiveCampus is a digital-first fundraising and alumni-engagement platform built for educational institutions - K-12 schools, colleges, universities, and their affiliated foundations, alumni associations, and nonprofits. The platform provides online giving pages, Giving Days, crowdfunding and peer-to-peer (advocacy) fundraising, matching and challenge gifts, event and volunteer management, donor management and advancement CRM tooling, payment processing, and stewardship and engagement features that help advancement teams raise more money at a lower cost. Founded in 2015 and backed by Y Combinator, GiveCampus is used by thousands of schools and institutions across the United States and internationally. This API Evangelist profile tracks GiveCampus as a company in the network; the company operates a closed SaaS product and does not publish a public developer API, so this record is identity- and infrastructure-focused.

providers.name: Verra
providers.description: Verra is a Washington, D.C.-based nonprofit standards body that develops and manages the world's leading certification programs for climate action and sustainable development. Its flagship program, the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS), is the most widely used voluntary greenhouse gas crediting program globally, with more than 2,579 registered projects across 132+ countries and over 1.3 billion Verified Carbon Units (VCUs) issued. Verra also operates the Climate, Community & Biodiversity Standards (CCB), the Sustainable Development Verified Impact Standard (SD VISta), the Plastic Waste Reduction Standard (PWRP), the Scope 3 Standard Program, and the Jurisdictional and Nested REDD+ (JNR) framework. The Verra Registry at registry.verra.org is the system of record for projects, methodologies, issuances, retirements, and the AFOLU pooled buffer account across these programs; project documentation, public comment periods, and credit-lifecycle records are all surfaced through that registry. Verra recently launched VCS Version 5, modernizing program operations, strengthening safeguards, and clarifying credit rights. Verra does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or GitHub organization; programmatic data access is limited to the registry's web interface and filtered report exports, and there is no open-source code or machine-readable spec catalog associated with the organization.

providers.name: Elwyn
providers.description: Elwyn is a Pennsylvania-headquartered nonprofit human services organization founded in 1852, providing services to children and adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities, autism, and behavioral health needs. Elwyn describes itself as "the longest-running human services nonprofit of its kind in the nation," operating across Pennsylvania, Delaware, New Jersey, and California with approximately 4,000 employees. The organization delivers six core service lines: Adult Behavioral Health Services, Children's Behavioral Health Services, Crisis Services, Early Learning Services, Educational Services, and Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities Services. Elwyn is a service-delivery nonprofit, not a software or API provider. It publishes no public APIs, OpenAPI documents, SDKs, developer portal, or open-data feeds. Its digital presence is limited to its marketing site (elwyn.org), program pages, news, and donation/contact forms. This profile documents the organization's mission and the absence of any public API or developer surface.

providers.name: GetCalFresh
providers.description: GetCalFresh is a service delivered by Code for America on behalf of the people of California, providing plain-language guidance to help Californians understand and navigate CalFresh (SNAP) food benefits. Since California's statewide move to BenefitsCal.com on the CalSAWS platform, GetCalFresh.org no longer accepts applications directly - it is an informational and guidance site that hands off to BenefitsCal and county agencies for eligibility determination and case processing. No public developer API is documented; historically, before BenefitsCal existed, Code for America's application tooling submitted CalFresh applications to county systems via generated PDF forms, fax, and secure email rather than a documented API.

providers.name: Sirum
providers.description: SIRUM (Supporting Initiatives to Redistribute Unused Medicine) is a nonprofit and the country's largest redistributor of surplus prescription medication. It connects unused, in-date medicine from manufacturers, wholesalers, pharmacies, and nursing homes with patients who cannot afford their prescriptions, operating under drug-donation laws across the United States. SIRUM runs a logistics and matching platform that routes donated medication to community partners and individuals in need, aiming to close the gap for the tens of millions of Americans who skip prescribed medication because of cost. Surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Human DX
providers.description: The Human Diagnosis Project (Human Dx) is a nonprofit initiative building an open, global medical intelligence system that combines the collective insight of physicians with machine learning to help make high-quality, affordable healthcare accessible to everyone. Its programs pair clinical microlearning and training tools for medical trainees with a specialist eConsult network that connects safety-net and underserved patients and their primary-care providers to volunteer specialists. The organization operates under the tagline "Rise together." Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Immunity Project
providers.description: Immunity Project was a San Francisco nonprofit and Y Combinator company (batch Winter 2014, one of YC's first non-profits alongside Watsi) that set out to develop a free HIV/AIDS vaccine. Its approach studied naturally immune "HIV controllers" and applied machine learning to reverse-engineer the immune response, aiming to deliver a crowdfunded, virus-free vaccine via nasal spray. Founders included Reid Rubsamen, Naveen Jain, and Ian Cinnamon. The organization surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Y Combinator portfolio lead; enrichment found no developer portal, documentation, or API surface, and its former domain (immunityproject.org) has lapsed and now redirects to an unrelated third-party news outlet, indicating the project is effectively defunct.

providers.name: Opencurriculum
providers.description: OpenCurriculum is a nonprofit education-technology organization (a Y Combinator alum) that builds curriculum-planning software for K-12 schools. Its web application helps teachers and administrators create and organize lesson plans, unit plans, and courses; draw on a curated library of high-quality, ready-to-go teaching ideas, resources, and strategies; align instruction to standards and learning goals; collaborate with colleagues on instructional design; and track progress through planner, calendar, and semester views with alignment analytics. The organization is based in Sacramento, California. As of this enrichment pass OpenCurriculum publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, OpenAPI specification, webhooks, or /.well-known discovery surface; it maintains a small public GitHub organization (one public repository, "flow", an open-source learning-app maker). This profile therefore carries company identity only, with no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: CrowdRise
providers.description: CrowdRise was an online fundraising platform for charities, nonprofits, and personal causes, founded around 2010 by Edward Norton and Robert Wolfe. It let individuals, event participants, and organizations create fundraising pages, run peer-to-peer campaigns, and collect donations for good. CrowdRise was acquired by GoFundMe in 2017 and subsequently merged into the GoFundMe platform; the crowdrise.com domain now 301-redirects to gofundme.com/c/crowdrise. This profile originated as a Union Square Ventures portfolio lead; no independent developer portal, documented API, SDKs, or discovery surface remains, so the record is retained for provenance only.

providers.name: Funderful
providers.description: Funderful was an alumni fundraising software platform for universities and higher-education advancement teams, founded in 2013 by Raimonds Kulbergs and headquartered in Riga, Latvia. It helped advancement offices run donation campaigns, track donors, and pioneer conversational chatbots to re-engage alumni, with clients including UC Berkeley, Georgetown, London Business School, and Oxford and Cambridge colleges. Funderful joined 500 Startups (Batch 20) and raised seed funding before being acquired by Ruffalo Noel Levitz (RNL) in February 2019. The company is defunct as an independent entity and its domain (funderful.com) no longer resolves; enrichment found no live developer portal, documentation, or public API surface.

providers.name: Make School
providers.description: Make School was a San Francisco-based computer science college and coding bootcamp, backed by a16z, that offered an applied computer science bachelor's program. As of August 2021 the degree program moved to Dominican University of California, and Make School.org now operates as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit running a scholarship program for former Bachelor in Applied Computer Science students. The organization publishes no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and this enrichment pass confirmed there is no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Capital.xyz
providers.description: Capital.xyz (the company behind the former Party Round) is a startup banking and fundraising platform that helps founders raise, hold, spend, and send money in one place. Companies sign up to run fundraising rounds, receive a virtual Visa debit card once capital is raised, hold and move funds, and connect the account to fintech services such as Gusto. The product is built on embedded-finance rails (Unit, Plaid, Visa) and is a consumer/SMB-facing application; as of this enrichment pass Capital.xyz publishes no public developer program, API reference, OpenAPI, or docs portal. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of a16z.
